messages:
maria.g: Heads up — after rolling kernel-v2 on eu-west we see a persistent drop in prefix cache hit-rate for eu-west (p50 hit-rate down ~18%) and a small but visible tail latency regression on the text-gen path. initial telemetry: kv_cache hit p50 72% -> 54% in eu-west, overall p99 latency +40ms. anyone seen similar after kernel changes?
sam.k: saw the spike too. looks correlated with kernel-v2's change to fused attention matmul path (faster when batch>16, worse for tiny batches). eu-west traffic has more small sessions so batching heuristics might be undersizing.
wayne: quick profiling dump i ran on a repro:```
# local perf summary (token loop)
kernel-v1: matmul 8.2ms, kv_get 0.9ms, total gen 39ms
kernel-v2: matmul 5.1ms, kv_get 1.8ms, total gen 83ms (small batches)
kv_cache.get p50 0.9ms p95 4.2ms p99 18.1ms
```
lee_ops: interesting — kv_get regression with kernel-v2. is kv cache local to process or does kernel-v2 change memory layout causing cache misses?
nana-ml: typo: it's ana-ml 😉 my hunch is twofold: (1) kernel-v2 changed tensor alignment so batched KV lookups go through a slower path, (2) our batcher window is shorter in eu-west due to the regional router sending micro-bursts to local edges. also replication lag means some prefixes aren't present locally, causing extra remote fetches.
maria.g: good points. can we get a trace that ties a cache miss to a remote replica fetch? deploy-bot: recorded request-trace 1855550123 for trace-id t-7f9a (linked)
sam.k: pulled the trace — when kv miss occurs we see a 12ms RTT to remote-origin + extra copy cost. root cause seems to be cache key normalization mismatch in one path: kernel-v2's tokenizer emits different trailing-space tokens for some prompts, so keys look different across regions.
wayne: that would explain inconsistent replication hits. sample keys:```
"prompt:what is the weather?"
"prompt:what is the weather?\n"  <-- kernel-v1 normalized strip, kernel-v2 didn't
```
lee_ops: wow. that's subtle. So fixes: normalize tokens at cache layer (server-side canonicalization) OR make kernel tokenization deterministic across variants. which is faster to land?
nana-ml: server-side canonicalization + a short migration (backfill) seems quickest. we can implement prefix-hash normalization: collapse trailing whitespace, normalize unicode NFKC, lower-case for non-sensitive routes. then compute consistent hash across regions.
maria.g: while that's in flight, can we mitigate by routing cold-region traffic to a warmed regional pool? tradeoff is cross-region latency. propose: if region hit-rate < 60% for 5m, route new requests to secondary warmed pool in nearest warm region, with a config flag per org.
sam.k: +1 for automated short-circuit. Also tweak batcher to prefer batching window extension in low-throughput zones: increase max wait by 20ms or allow cross-tenant micro-batching when safe. This could push batch sizes to the kernel-v2 sweet spot.
wayne: created a small benchmark that shows batcher wait +20ms increases mean batch size from 6->14 in eu-west, matmul latency then drops and total gen recovers. next step: AB test rate-limited extension on a single canary shard.
lee_ops: action items I can take: (1) deploy server-side key normalization in canary; (2) start priming job to replicate top-50K prefixes from global hotset into eu-west cache (best-effort, async); (3) add a routing rule to prefer warmed pool when region hit-rate < threshold.
nana-ml: i'll add an instrumentation metric: prefix_key_version tag + pre/post normalization sample in traces so we can verify how many keys were mismatched historically. also add kernel variant tag to traces so we can measure hit-rate by kernel.
maria.g: plan looks good. timeline? lee_ops?
lee_ops: canary normalization deploy today (non-breaking), priming job to run within 2 hours, routing rule behind a feature-flag to test tomorrow. batcher tweak PR from sam for review now.
sam.k: PR posted: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/4321 — it includes opt-in batcher extension + cross-tenant collapse when safe. please review.
wayne: i'll run a 6-hour perf run comparing kernel-v1/v2 with normalization on/off and post numeric heatmap.
maria.g: thanks all. let's reconvene after the canary window — if normalization fixes >10% hit-rate we'll keep kernel-v2, otherwise consider rolling back kernel on eu-west. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy log: canary normalization service v1.1 rolled to eu-west-canary at 2026-03-18T14:22:03Z (id dc-9812)
